# Code instructions

The `.code` stack holds code blocks: lists of any items, nested to any depth. A code block met on `.exec` comes to rest here as data; `.codeDo` and the other control instructions are what run one. Code blocks are also the language's general-purpose container.

<!-- Generated by Instruction Reference Tests from the language itself: do not edit. -->

## Operations

| Instruction | What it does | Takes | Gives |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.codeConcat` | Concatenates two code blocks' root items: `( a ) ( b c ) .codeConcat` gives `( a b c )`. | `code`, `code` | `code` |
| `.codeContainer` | Copies the code block directly holding n's first occurrence in h, leaving both: `h n .codeContainer`; refuses if n is absent or is h itself. | `code` (read), `code` (read) | `code`; may refuse |
| `.codeContains` | Tests whether code block n occurs as a point of code block h, leaving both: `h n .codeContains`; a one-item n stands for its sole item. | `code` (read), `code` (read) | `bool` |
| `.codeCutAtGap` | Splits the whole tree at gap i (clamped), front part beneath, back on top; leaves keep their order, and code blocks the cut crosses split in two. | `code`, `int` | `code`, `code` |
| `.codeCutRoot` | Splits a code block's root items at gap i, clamped to 0 through their count: the front part beneath, the back part on top. | `code`, `int` | `code`, `code` |
| `.codeDepth` | Measures how deeply code blocks nest, leaving the code block: `( )` is 0, a flat code block 1, each nested level one more. | `code` (read) | `int` |
| `.codeDifference` | Filters: `a b .codeDifference` keeps the items of code block a that do not occur in b, compared by value, in a's order, repeats included. | `code`, `code` | `code` |
| `.codeDistinct` | Removes repeated items from a code block, comparing by value and keeping each first occurrence in order. | `code` | `code` |
| `.codeDropRoot` | Drops the front: `( … ) n .codeDropRoot` removes the first n root items, n clamped to 0 through the length. | `code`, `int` | `code` |
| `.codeEq` | Pushes whether the top two code blocks are equal, leaving both. | `code` (read), `code` (read) | `bool` |
| `.codeFindPrefix` | Finds a nested code block: `( … ) ( p ) .codeFindPrefix` gives the first root item that is a code block beginning with p's items, and its index; refuses on a miss. | `code` (read), `code` (read) | `code`, `int`; may refuse |
| `.codeFindPrefixFrom` | Finds a nested code block from root index i on: `( … ) ( p ) i .codeFindPrefixFrom` gives the first that begins with p's items, and its index; refuses on a miss. | `code` (read), `code` (read), `int` (read) | `code`, `int`; may refuse |
| `.codeFirstRoot` | Takes a code block's first root item as a code block; a leaf comes boxed as `( x )`; refuses an empty code block. | `code` | `code`; may refuse |
| `.codeFlatten` | Flattens a code block to its leaves, in order; nested empty code blocks vanish. | `code` | `code` |
| `.codeFlattenNth` | Flattens the subtree at point i (clamped) in place; a leaf point is unchanged, and point 0 flattens everything. | `code`, `int` | `code` |
| `.codeFlattenOnce` | Flattens one level: each root item that is a code block is replaced by its items. | `code` | `code` |
| `.codeFlattenRange` | Flattens every code block whose first or last gap lies between gaps i and j (clamped, either order); code blocks enclosing the range keep their shape. | `code`, `int`, `int` | `code` |
| `.codeFromFunction` | A function's body as a code block, its holes left out: run, each hole is an argument its instructions take from the stacks. | `function` | `code` |
| `.codeFromIterator` | Collects everything the iterator has left to emit into one code block, its body returning to `.code` beneath; refuses, keeping the iterator, when that is too many items. | `iterator` | `code` or `code`, `code`; may refuse |
| `.codeIndexOf` | Finds the first point of h equal to n, leaving both: `h n .codeIndexOf`; a one-item n stands for its sole item; refuses when absent. | `code` (read), `code` (read) | `int`; may refuse |
| `.codeInsertAtGap` | Inserts: `s x i .codeInsertAtGap` splices code block x into s at gap i (clamped); a one-item x inserts its sole item. | `code`, `code`, `int` | `code` |
| `.codeIntersect` | Filters: `a b .codeIntersect` keeps the items of code block a that also occur in b, compared by value, in a's order, repeats included. | `code`, `code` | `code` |
| `.codeIsSubset` | Tells whether every item of code block a occurs in code block b, compared by value: `a b .codeIsSubset`, leaving both. | `code` (read), `code` (read) | `bool` |
| `.codeItemIsEmpty` | Tests whether the code block has no items, leaving the code block. | `code` (read) | `bool` |
| `.codeLastRoot` | Takes a code block's last root item as a code block; a leaf comes boxed as `( x )`; refuses an empty code block. | `code` | `code`; may refuse |
| `.codeLength` | Counts the code block's points, the code block itself included, leaving the code block: `( ( 1 2 ) 3 )` has 5. | `code` (read) | `int` |
| `.codeLengthRoot` | Counts the code block's root items, leaving the code block. | `code` (read) | `int` |
| `.codeNth` | Takes point i (clamped) as a code block; a leaf comes boxed as `( x )`. | `code`, `int` | `code` |
| `.codeNthRoot` | Takes root item i (clamped) as a code block; a leaf comes boxed as `( x )`; refuses an empty code block. | `code`, `int` | `code`; may refuse |
| `.codeOccurrencesOf` | Counts the points of h equal to n, leaving both: `h n .codeOccurrencesOf`; a one-item n stands for its sole item. | `code` (read), `code` (read) | `int` |
| `.codePair` | Pairs two code blocks into one: `( a ) ( b c ) .codePair` gives `( a ( b c ) )`, a one-item code block contributing its sole item. | `code`, `code` | `code` |
| `.codePeekNth` | Copies point i (clamped) as a code block, leaving the code block and index; a leaf comes boxed as `( x )`. | `code` (read), `int` (read) | `code` |
| `.codePeekNthRoot` | Copies root item i (clamped) as a code block, leaving the code block and index; a leaf comes boxed as `( x )`; refuses an empty code block. | `code` (read), `int` (read) | `code`; may refuse |
| `.codePushAllFunctions` | Takes a code block and pushes every function its pushes compute: the code block runs with a placeholder for each missing argument, and each item it makes from a placeholder becomes a function with a hole there; refuses a code block that runs too long. | `code` | `function`, any number; may refuse |
| `.codeRefAs` | Binds the top code block to key k from `.int`, taking both and shadowing any older binding of k: `x k .codeRefAs`. | `code`, `int` | `binding` |
| `.codeRemoveNth` | Removes point i (clamped) with everything under it; removing point 0 gives `( )`. | `code`, `int` | `code` |
| `.codeReplace` | Replaces matching points: `s n r .codeReplace` puts r for every point of s equal to n; a one-item n or r stands for its item. | `code`, `code`, `code` | `code` |
| `.codeReplaceFirst` | Replaces the first matching point: `s n r .codeReplaceFirst` puts r for s's first point equal to n; a one-item n or r stands for its item. | `code`, `code`, `code` | `code` |
| `.codeReverseRoot` | Reverses the order of a code block's root items. | `code` | `code` |
| `.codeTakeRoot` | Keeps the front: `( … ) n .codeTakeRoot` gives the first n root items, n clamped to 0 through the length. | `code`, `int` | `code` |
| `.codeWidth` | Counts the code block's leaves (items that are not code blocks) at every depth, leaving the code block. | `code` (read) | `int` |
| `.codeWrap` | Wraps a code block in another: `( a b )` becomes `( ( a b ) )`. | `code` | `code` |
| `.codeWrapRange` | Wraps everything between gaps i and j (clamped, either order) in a new code block; equal gaps insert `( )`, and crossed code block edges are repaired. | `code`, `int`, `int` | `code` |
| `.vecFromCode` | Turns a code block of bools, ints, doubles or strings, all one type, into a vector; a code block holding one vector gives it back; refuses anything else. | `code` | `vecBool` or `vecDouble` or `vecInt` or `vecString`; may refuse |

## Reading the environment

| Instruction | What it does | Takes | Gives |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.codeLookupContaining` | Reads the top code block as a probe and copies the topmost one below containing it, or its lone item, anywhere inside, pushing its depth + 1 onto `.int`; refuses on a miss. | `code` (read) | `code`, `int`; may refuse |
| `.codeLookupContainingFrom` | Reads the top code block as a probe and copies the topmost one below containing it, or its lone item, anywhere inside, searching from depth i (at least 1), pushing its depth + 1 onto `.int`; refuses on a miss. | `int`, `code` (read) | `code`, `int`; may refuse |
| `.codeLookupEqual` | Reads the top code block as a probe and copies the topmost one below that equals it, pushing its depth + 1 onto `.int`; refuses on a miss. | `code` (read) | `code`, `int`; may refuse |
| `.codeLookupEqualFrom` | Reads the top code block as a probe and copies the topmost one below that equals it, searching from depth i (at least 1), pushing its depth + 1 onto `.int`; refuses on a miss. | `int`, `code` (read) | `code`, `int`; may refuse |
| `.codeLookupPrefix` | Reads the top code block as a probe and copies the topmost one below whose items begin with its items, pushing its depth + 1 onto `.int`; refuses on a miss. | `code` (read) | `code`, `int`; may refuse |
| `.codeLookupPrefixFrom` | Reads the top code block as a probe and copies the topmost one below whose items begin with its items, searching from depth i (at least 1), pushing its depth + 1 onto `.int`; refuses on a miss. | `int`, `code` (read) | `code`, `int`; may refuse |
| `.codeLookupShape` | Reads the top code block as a probe and copies the topmost one below with its shape (same nesting and instructions, atoms matching by type), pushing its depth + 1 onto `.int`; refuses on a miss. | `code` (read) | `code`, `int`; may refuse |
| `.codeLookupShapeFrom` | Reads the top code block as a probe and copies the topmost one below with its shape (same nesting and instructions, atoms matching by type), searching from depth i (at least 1), pushing its depth + 1 onto `.int`; refuses on a miss. | `int`, `code` (read) | `code`, `int`; may refuse |
| `.codeRef` | Binds a copy of the top code block, left in place, to a fresh key and pushes the key onto `.int`. | `code` (read) | `binding`, `int` |

## Control

| Instruction | What it does | Takes | Gives |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.codeDo` | Runs a code block: its items go onto `.exec`, the first to run first. | `code` | the rest of the program |
| `.codeDoIf` | Runs the code block as `.codeDo` would if the bool is true; otherwise does nothing, leaving the code block on `.code`. `.execWhen` discards it instead. | `bool`, `code` | the rest of the program |
| `.codeDoNth` | Runs point i (clamped), leaving the code block and index: a nested code block's contents execute, a leaf goes to its stack. | `code` (read), `int` (read) | the rest of the program |
| `.codeDoNthRoot` | Runs root item i (clamped), leaving the code block and index: a nested code block's contents execute; refuses an empty code block. | `code` (read), `int` (read) | the rest of the program; may refuse |
| `.codeEmitNth` | Sends point i (clamped) to `.exec` as it is, leaving the code block and index: a nested code block lands on `.code`, an instruction runs. | `code` (read), `int` (read) | the rest of the program |
| `.codeEmitNthRoot` | Sends root item i (clamped) to `.exec` as it is, leaving the code block and index; refuses an empty code block. | `code` (read), `int` (read) | the rest of the program; may refuse |
| `.codeIterate` | Loops: `x b .codeIterate` runs code block b once per point of code block x, root first, pushing each point as a code block; b ends on `.code`. | `code`, `code` | the rest of the program |
| `.codeIterateDo` | Loops: `x b .codeIterateDo` runs code block b once per point of code block x, root first, also running each point; b ends on `.code`. | `code`, `code` | the rest of the program |
| `.codeIterateEmit` | Loops: `x b .codeIterateEmit` runs code block b once per point of code block x, root first, pushing each point as it is (an instruction runs); b ends on `.code`. | `code`, `code` | the rest of the program |
| `.codeIterateRoot` | Loops: `x b .codeIterateRoot` runs code block b once per root item of code block x, pushing each item to its stack (an instruction runs); b ends on `.code`. | `code`, `code` | the rest of the program |
| `.codeWith` | Binds a copy of the code block under the body to a fresh key, runs a body code block from `.code` with the key on `.int`, then removes the binding. | `code`, `code` (read) | the rest of the program |

## Output

| Instruction | What it does | Takes | Gives |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.codePrint` | Prints the top code block and a newline to the output. | `code` | the printout |

## The stack's own instructions

Every stack has the same family for copying, deleting, reordering and measuring its items; see <doc:StackInstructions>. On `.code` they are `.codeDeepDup`, `.codeDeleteAtDepth`, `.codeDup`, `.codeDupItems`, `.codeDupTimes`, `.codeFlush`, `.codePop`, `.codePopItems`, `.codeRot`, `.codeShove`, `.codeStackDepth`, `.codeStackIsEmpty`, `.codeSwap`, `.codeYank`, `.codeYankDup`.
